label: tA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{tA}
Let $G$ be an infinite finitely generated group and $P$ a symmetric finitely supported probability measure whose support generates $G$. Then $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ for every $n$ with $L(n) \geq 1$.
head: environment

label: tB
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{tB}
Let $X$ be a graph and $\mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(v) := \inf\{ |\ensuremath{\partial} F|/|F| \mid 0 < |F| \leq v\}$ its decreasing isoperimetric ratio function. For every finitely supported $f : X 	o [0,1]$ with $\|f\|_{\ell^1} = 1$,
\[
\|
abla f\|_{\ell^1} \; \geq \; 	frac14\, \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}} ig(2e^{2H(f)} ig),
\]
and $\|
abla f\|_{\ell^1} \geq 	frac12\, \psi ig(H(f) ig)$ for every convex non-increasing $\psi$ with $\psi(u) \leq \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(2e^u)$. In particular, if $X$ has $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$ then $\|
abla f\|_{\ell^1} \geq  rac K2  ig(1 + \ln 2 + H(f) ig)^{-1/
u}$, and for a symmetric random walk on a Cayley graph with $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$ one has $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq H(P^n)^{-1/
u}$.
head: environment

label: lweightedtc
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\mu_\pm$ for the positive and negative parts of $\lambda_s\eta - \eta$; they
have the same total mass $M$. Leave the common mass in place and route everything else through the identity: the product
coupling $m(x,y) = \mu_+(x)\mu_-(y)/M$ has the required marginals and, since
$d(x,y) = |x^{-1}y| \leq |x| + |y|$, a cost of at most
$\sum_x |x|\mu_+(x) + \sum_y |y|\mu_-(y)$.
For the case $\eta = P^n$, note that $\lambda_s P^n = \delta_s * P^n$. It remains to see that \eqref{ecritrelax} forces $\mathrm{TV}_n \to 0$, so that $P^n$ does tend to an invariant mean: restricting the sum to $|x| \geq r$ gives $K \geq r\big(2\mathrm{TV}_n - 2P^n(B_r)\big)$, and $P^n(B_r) \to 0$ for every fixed $r$ as $G$ is infinite.
head: environment

label: rholder
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rholder}
H\"older's inequality, with $\tfrac1p + \tfrac1q = 1$
and $M_p(n) := \overset{}{\underset{x}{\sum}}|x|^p|\delta_s * P^n(x) - P^n(x)|$, can be used to get
\[
\mathrm{TC}\big(\lambda_s P^n, P^n\big) \; \leq \; \overset{}{\underset{x}{\sum}} |x|\,
\big|\delta_s * P^n(x) - P^n(x)\big| \; \leq \; M_p(n)^{1/p} \,
\big(2\mathrm{TV}_n\big)^{1/q} .
\]
But this does not help if $M_p$ is estimated simply by $M_p(n) \preceq \mathbbold{E}|P^n|^p$. Even in Abelian groups, where it can be checked that the random walk distributions yield a sequence of measures for which the group is transport amenable, the estimate $M_p(n) \preceq \mathbbold{E}|P^n|^p$ is too crude.
head: environment

label: prevpinsker
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prevpinsker}
Let $P$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $G$ with $\mathrm{supp}\,P \subseteq S \cup \{\mathfr{o}\}$. Then, for every $n \geq 0$,
\[
H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n) \; \leq \; 4\,|\mathrm{supp}\,P|\; \mathrm{TV}_n .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Y_1, Y_2, \ldots$ be independent random elements of $G$ with law $P$, and let $X_k := Y_1 \cdots Y_k$ (with $X_0 := \mathfr{o}$), so that $X_k$ has law $P^k$. Throughout, write
\[
\mu_s := \delta_s * P^n \quad (s \in \mathrm{supp}\,P) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \nu := P^{n+1},
\]
and recall that $\|\mu - \mu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}} = \tfrac12 \|\mu - \mu'\|_{\ell^1G}$.

\emph{Step 1: the increment is a mutual information.} We use the standard notions of Cover \& Thomas \cite[Ch.~2]{CoverThomas}. For random variables $U$ and $V$ with values in countable sets, with joint law $p(u,v)$, marginal laws $p(u)$ and $p(v)$, and conditional laws $p(v \mid u) = p(u,v)/p(u)$, the conditional entropy is $H(V \mid U) := \sum_u p(u)\, H\big(p(\cdot \mid u)\big)$ and the {\bfseries mutual information} is $I(U;V) := H(V) - H(V \mid U)$. Writing $H(V) = -\sum_{u,v} p(u,v) \ln p(v)$, one gets
\[
I(U;V) = \sum_{u,v} p(u,v) \ln \frac{p(v \mid u)}{p(v)} = \sum_u p(u)\, D\big(p(\cdot \mid u) \,\|\, p(\cdot)\big),
\]
where $D(\mu \,\|\, \nu) := \sum_v \mu(v) \ln \frac{\mu(v)}{\nu(v)}$ is the {\bfseries Kullback--Leibler divergence}: the mutual information is the average divergence of the conditional laws of $V$ from its law.

Apply this to $U = X_1$ and $V = X_{n+1}$. One has $X_{n+1} = X_1 Z$ where $Z := Y_2 \cdots Y_{n+1}$ has law $P^n$ and is independent of $X_1 = Y_1$. Hence, conditionally on $X_1 = s$, the law of $X_{n+1}$ is $\mu_s$. Its entropy is $H(P^n)$, because $z \mapsto sz$ is a bijection of $G$ and the entropy of a measure is invariant under bijections. Therefore $H(X_{n+1} \mid X_1) = \sum_s P(s)\, H(\mu_s) = H(P^n)$, and
\[
H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n) = I(X_1 ; X_{n+1}) = \sum_{s} P(s)\, D(\mu_s \,\|\, \nu).
\]

\emph{Step 2: the likelihood ratios are bounded.} Since $\nu = P * P^n = \sum_t P(t)\, \mu_t$ is a sum of non-negative terms, one has $\nu \geq P(s)\, \mu_s$ pointwise. Hence $\mu_s$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\nu$, and its density $r_s := \mu_s / \nu$ (defined on the support of $\nu$, which contains that of $\mu_s$) takes values in $[0, 1/P(s)]$. In particular the divergences of Step 1 are finite.

\emph{Step 3: divergence versus $\chi^2$.} Steps 3 and 4 are standard: Step 3 is the classical bound of the Kullback--Leibler divergence by the $\chi^2$-divergence (see \emph{e.g.}  Tsybakov \cite[\S{}2.4]{Tsybakov}), and Steps 2--4 together are an instance of the reverse Pinsker inequalities for measures with bounded relative density (see \emph{e.g.}  Sason \& Verd\'u \cite{SV}); we include the short arguments for completeness. Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures with $\mu = r\nu$. The inequality $\ln u \leq u - 1$, applied at every point where $\mu(x) > 0$, gives
\[
D(\mu \,\|\, \nu) = \sum_x \mu(x) \ln r(x) \; \leq \; \sum_x \mu(x)\big(r(x) - 1\big) = \sum_x \nu(x)\big(r(x)-1\big)^2 + \sum_x \nu(x) \big(r(x) - 1\big),
\]
where the equality uses $\mu = r\nu$ and $r(r-1) = (r-1)^2 + (r-1)$. The last sum is $\mu(G) - \nu(G) = 0$, so that
\[
D(\mu \,\|\, \nu) \; \leq \; \sum_x \nu(x) \big( r(x) - 1\big)^2 .
\]

\emph{Step 4: $\chi^2$ versus total variation.} Bounding one of the two factors $|r - 1|$ by its supremum,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_x \nu(x)\big(r(x) - 1\big)^2 \; & \leq \; \|r - 1\|_{\ell^\infty} \sum_x \nu(x)\, |r(x) - 1| \\
& = \|r - 1\|_{\ell^\infty}\, \|\mu - \nu\|_{\ell^1G} = 2\, \|r-1\|_{\ell^\infty}\, \|\mu - \nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}} .
\end{aligned}
\]
For $\mu = \mu_s$, Step 2 gives $\|r_s - 1\|_{\ell^\infty} \leq \max\big(1, 1/P(s) - 1\big) \leq 1/P(s)$. Together with Step 3,
\[
D(\mu_s \,\|\, \nu) \; \leq \; \frac{2}{P(s)}\, \|\mu_s - \nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}} .
\]

\emph{Step 5: comparison with the total variation profile.} Since $\nu = \sum_t P(t)\,\mu_t$ and the total variation distance is convex in each variable,
\[
\|\mu_s - \nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \; \leq \; \sum_t P(t)\, \|\mu_s - \mu_t\|_{\mathrm{TV}} .
\]
The bijection $x \mapsto t^{-1}x$ preserves the total variation distance and maps $\mu_s$ and $\mu_t$ to $\delta_g * P^n$ and $P^n$, where $g := t^{-1}s$. As $s,t \in S \cup \{\mathfr{o}\}$, one has $|g| \leq 2$. Writing $g = u_1 \cdots u_k$ with $k = |g|$ and $u_i \in S$, the triangle inequality and the same invariance give
\[
\big\|\delta_g * P^n - P^n\big\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \; \leq \; \overset{k}{\underset{i=1}{\sum}} \big\| \delta_{u_1 \cdots u_i} * P^n - \delta_{u_1 \cdots u_{i-1}} * P^n \big\|_{\mathrm{TV}} = \overset{k}{\underset{i=1}{\sum}} \big\| \delta_{u_i} * P^n - P^n \big\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \; \leq \; 2\, \mathrm{TV}_n .
\]
Hence $\|\mu_s - \nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \leq 2\,\mathrm{TV}_n$ for every $s \in \mathrm{supp}\,P$.

\emph{Conclusion.} By Steps 1, 4 and 5,
\[
\begin{aligned}[b]
H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n) & = \sum_{s \in \mathrm{supp}\,P} P(s)\, D(\mu_s \,\|\, \nu) \\
& \leq \; \sum_{s \in \mathrm{supp}\,P} P(s) \cdot \frac{2}{P(s)} \cdot 2\, \mathrm{TV}_n = 4\, |\mathrm{supp}\,P|\, \mathrm{TV}_n .
\end{aligned} \qedhere
\]
head: environment

label: crevpinsker
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{crevpinsker}
Let $h := \lim_n \tfrac1n H(P^n)$ be the asymptotic entropy of the walk. Then $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq h / (4|\mathrm{supp}\,P|)$ for every $n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The increments $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$ are non-increasing (see above), and a non-increasing sequence whose Ces\`aro means tend to $h$ is bounded below by $h$. Apply Proposition \ref{prevpinsker}.
head: environment

label: lretgrowth
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lretgrowth}
Let $m \geq 1$, let $N \geq 0$ be even, and let $\Phi(v) := \min\{ r \mid |B_r| > v\}$. Then
\[
\mathrm{TV}_m \; \geq \; \frac{P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})}{4\,P^N(\mathfr{o})\,
\big(\Phi\big(2/P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})\big)+1\big)} \, .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $P$ is symmetric, $P^{N+m}(\gamma) = \langle  P^N \mid \lambda_\gamma P^m \rangle$ for every $\gamma$, so
\[
P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o}) - P^{N+m}(\gamma) = \langle P^N \mid P^m - \lambda_\gamma P^m \rangle
\leq \|P^N\|_{\ell^\infty} \big\|P^m - \lambda_\gamma P^m\big\|_{\ell^1}
\leq 2|\gamma| \, P^N(\mathfr{o}) \, \mathrm{TV}_m ,
\]
using $\|P^N\|_{\ell^\infty} = P^N(\mathfr{o})$, valid for $N$ even because $P^N(x) = \langle P^{N/2}\delta_x \mid P^{N/2}\delta_{\mathfr{o}} \rangle \leq P^N(\mathfr{o})$ by Cauchy--Schwarz, and the telescoping bound $\|P^m - \lambda_\gamma P^m\|_{\ell^1} \leq |\gamma| \textrm{\raisebox{.5ex}{\mbox{$\underset{s \in S}{\max}$}}} \:\|P^m - \lambda_s P^m\|_{\ell^1}$.
Set $k := \lfloor P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o}) / \big(4P^N(\mathfr{o})\mathrm{TV}_m\big)\rfloor$.
For $|\gamma| \leq k$ the right-hand side is at most $\tfrac12 P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})$, so $P^{N+m}(\gamma) \geq \tfrac12 P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})$, and summing over $B_k$ gives $1 \geq \tfrac12 |B_k| P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})$, \emph{i.e.}  $|B_k| \leq 2/P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})$.
Hence $k \leq \Phi(2/P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o}))$, which is the claim.
head: environment

label: cretgrowth
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cretgrowth}
Write $u(N) := -\ln P^N(\mathfr{o})$. For every even $m \geq 2$ and every even $N$ with $N \geq m\,u(N)$,
\[
\mathrm{TV}_m \; \geq \; \frac{1}{4e\,\big(\Phi\big(2e^{1+u(N)}\big)+1\big)} \, .
\]
Since $\mathrm{TV}_n$ is non-increasing, the same holds for odd $m$ provided $N \geq (m+1)\,u(N)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Convolution by $P$ is a self-adjoint contraction of $\ell^2G$. If $\mu$ is the spectral measure of $\delta_{\mathfr{o}}$, then for even $t$ one has $P^t(\mathfr{o}) = \int_{[-1,1]} (\lambda^2)^{t/2} \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}}\mu(\lambda)$, and H\"older's inequality shows that $\psi(t) := \ln P^t(\mathfr{o})$ is convex on the even integers. (If $P$ is lazy, its spectrum lies in $[0,1]$ and $\psi$ is convex on all integers, but this is not needed.)
Since $\psi(0) = 0$, convexity gives $\psi(N+m) - \psi(N) \geq \tfrac{m}{N}\psi(N) = -m\,u(N)/N \geq -1$. Hence $P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o})/P^N(\mathfr{o}) \geq e^{-1}$ and $1/P^{N+m}(\mathfr{o}) \leq e^{1+u(N)}$, and the claim follows from Lemma \ref{lretgrowth} and the monotonicity of $\Phi$. For odd $m$, apply this to $m+1$.
head: environment

label: ptvspeed
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{ptvspeed}
For every $n$ with $L(n) \geq 1$ one has $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\varepsilon := 2\mathrm{TV}_n = \textrm{\raisebox{.5ex}{\mbox{$\underset{s\in S}{\max}$}}} \:\|\lambda_sP^n - P^n\|_{\ell^1}$. Writing
$\gamma = s_1 \cdots s_m$ as a geodesic word and telescoping, the left-invariance of
$\|\cdot\|_{\ell^1}$ gives
\[
\big\| \lambda_\gamma P^n - P^n \big\|_{\ell^1}
\leq \overset{m}{\underset{i=1}{\sum}} \big\| \lambda_{s_i}P^n - P^n\big\|_{\ell^1}
\leq |\gamma| \, \varepsilon .
\]
Let $R := \lceil 4L(n)\rceil$. Markov's inequality gives $P^n(B_R) \geq 3/4$.
Since $G$ is infinite there is $\gamma$ with $|\gamma| = 2R+1$, and then
$\gamma B_R \cap B_R = \varnothing$, as $\gamma B_R$ meets $B_R$ only if
$\gamma \in B_RB_R^{-1} = B_{2R}$. Now $\lambda_\gamma P^n(\gamma B_R) = P^n(B_R) \geq
3/4$, so
\[
P^n(\gamma B_R) \; \geq \; \tfrac34 - \big\|\lambda_\gamma P^n - P^n\big\|_{\ell^1}
\; \geq \; \tfrac34 - (2R+1)\varepsilon .
\]
The two sets being disjoint, $P^n(\gamma B_R) + P^n(B_R) \leq 1$, whence
$(2R+1)\varepsilon \geq \tfrac12$. As $L(n)\geq 1$ one has $2R+1 \leq 8L(n)+3 \leq
11L(n)$, so $\varepsilon \geq 1/\big(22L(n)\big)$, \emph{i.e.}  $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44L(n)\big)$.
head: environment

label: tiisent-p
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{tiisent-p}
Assume $X=(V,E)$ has $\mathrm{IIS}_\nu$ with constant $K$.
Then, for any finitely supported
$f:V \to [0,1]$ with
$\|f\|_{\ell^1V}=1$
and $\|f\|_{\ell^\infty} \leq \mathrm{exp}(-1)$,
\[
 \| \nabla f\|_1 \geq \frac{K\nu}{2^{1/\nu}(\nu+1)} H(f)^{-1/\nu} .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $[f>t] = \{ x \mid f(x)>t\}$ and by abuse of notation its cardinality too (likewise for $\ensuremath{\partial} [f>t]$).
By assumption, $f$ is not a Dirac mass. Note that
\[
\begin{array}{rll}
\| \nabla f \|_{\ell^1V}
&\displaystyle = \sum_x \sum_{y \sim x \mid f(y) > f(x) } f(y)-f(x) \\
&\displaystyle = \sum_x \sum_{y \sim x \mid f(y) > f(x) } \int_0^\infty \mathbbold{1}_{[f(x),f(y)[}(t) \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t \\
&\displaystyle = \int_0^\infty \sum_x \sum_{y \sim x \mid f(y) > t> f(x) } 1 \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t \\
&\displaystyle = \int_0^\infty \ensuremath{\partial} [f >t] \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t \\
&\displaystyle \overset{IS}\geq \int_0^\infty [f >t] / ( 1+\ln [f>t] )^{1/\nu} \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t\\
&\displaystyle \overset{MI}\geq 2^{-1/\nu} \int_0^1 [f >t] / ( -\ln t )^{1/\nu} \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t ,
\end{array}
\]
where IS is the use of $\mathrm{IIS}_\nu$ and MI is Markov's inequality $[f>t] \leq \|f\|_1/t= 1/t$. As $[f>t] = \varnothing$ for $t \geq e^{-1}$, only $t < e^{-1}$ matters; then $-\ln t > 1$, so that $1 + \ln [f>t] \leq 1 - \ln t \leq -2\ln t$ and $(1+\ln [f>t])^{-1/\nu} \geq 2^{-1/\nu}(-\ln t)^{-1/\nu}$. To lighten notation, the factor $K$ coming from $\mathrm{IIS}_\nu$ is omitted above, and so is the factor $2^{-1/\nu}K$ from now on; both are restored in the last line.

Since $\|f\|_\infty  \leq e^{-1}$, for $t\leq e^{-1}$, one has $-\ln t \geq 1$ so $\frac{1+1/\nu}{(-\ln t)^{1/\nu}} \geq \frac{1}{(-\ln t)^{1/\nu}} + \frac{1/\nu}{(-\ln t)^{1+1/\nu}}$.
Hence
\[
 \| \nabla f \|_1
 \geq \int_0^1 [f >t] / ( -\ln t )^{1/\nu} \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t
 \geq \frac{\nu}{\nu+1} \int_0^1 \bigg(\frac{1}{(-\ln t)^{1/\nu}} + \frac{1/\nu}{(-\ln t)^{1+1/\nu}} \bigg) [f >t] \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t ,
\]
that is,
\[
\| \nabla f \|_1
\geq \frac{\nu}{\nu+1} \int_0^1 \mathcal{H}(t)' [f >t] \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t ,
\]
where $\mathcal{H}(t) = t / (-\ln t)^{1/\nu}$.

Now, if $t_1 < \dots < t_n$ are the values taken by $f$ and $t_0 := 0$, then
\[
\begin{array}{rll}
\sum_x \frac{ f(x)}{(-\ln f(x) )^{1/\nu}}
&\displaystyle = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{t_i}{(-\ln  t_i)^{1/\nu}} ( [f>t_{i-1}] - [f>t_i]) \\
&\displaystyle = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \bigg( \frac{t_{i+1}}{(-\ln  t_{i+1})^{1/\nu}} - \frac{t_i}{(-\ln  t_i)^{1/\nu}} \bigg) [f>t_i]\\
&\displaystyle = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \int_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}} \mathcal{H}(t)' [f>t_i] \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t\\
&\displaystyle = \int_{0}^{1} \mathcal{H}(t)' [f>t] \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t .
\end{array}
\]
So
\[
\int_0^1 \mathcal{H}(t)' [f >t] \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t
= \sum_x f(x) \bigg(-\ln f(x) \bigg)^{-1/\nu}
\overset{\text{J}}{\geq} \bigg( \sum_x f(x) (-\ln f(x)) \bigg)^{-1/\nu} = H(f) ^{-1/\nu} ,
\]
where J stands for Jensen's inequality.
Indeed, as $\phi(x) = x^{-1/\nu}$ is convex, $\sum p_x \phi(a_x) \geq \phi( \sum p_x a_x)$.
Here, $p_x= f(x)$ and $a_x = -\ln f(x)$ were used.
Putting these inequalities together gives
\[
 \| \nabla f\|_1 \geq \frac{\nu}{2^{1/\nu}(\nu+1)} K H(f)^{-1/\nu} ,
\]
as desired.
head: environment

label: pentprofile
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $t > 0$ let $A_t := [f > t]$. As in the proof of Proposition \ref{tiisent-p}, the coarea formula gives $\|\nabla f\|_1 = \int_0^\infty |\ensuremath{\partial} A_t| \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t$. Since $\|f\|_{\ell^1} = 1$, Markov's inequality gives $|A_t| \leq 1/t$, and as $\mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}$ is non-increasing, $|\ensuremath{\partial} A_t| \geq \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(|A_t|)\,|A_t| \geq \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(1/t)\,|A_t|$. By Fubini (the sum runs over the support of $f$),
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
\|\nabla f\|_1 & \displaystyle \geq \; \int_0^\infty \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(1/t)\,|A_t| \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t & \displaystyle = \sum_x \int_0^{f(x)} \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(1/t) \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t \\
& \displaystyle \geq \; \sum_x \int_{f(x)/2}^{f(x)} \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(1/t) \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t & \displaystyle \geq \; \tfrac12 \sum_x f(x)\, \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}\big(2/f(x)\big),
\end{array}
\]
since $1/t \leq 2/f(x)$ on the last interval of integration.
Now let $Z$ be a random vertex with law $f$ and $Y := -\ln f(Z)$, a non-negative random variable with $\mathbbold{E}Y = H(f)$. With $\phi(u) := \mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(2e^u)$, which is non-increasing, the right-hand side above is $\tfrac12\mathbbold{E}\,\phi(Y)$.
For (a), Markov's inequality gives $\mathbbold{P}\big(Y \leq 2H(f)\big) \geq \tfrac12$, and $\phi(Y) \geq \phi(2H(f))$ on that event, so that $\mathbbold{E}\,\phi(Y) \geq \tfrac12\phi(2H(f))$.
For (b), $\mathbbold{E}\,\phi(Y) \geq \mathbbold{E}\,\psi(Y) \geq \psi(\mathbbold{E}Y)$ by Jensen's inequality.
head: environment

label: rentprofile
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rentprofile}
Two choices of $\psi$ recover the previous results. Under $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$ with constant $K$, the function $\psi(u) := K(1 + \ln 2 + u)^{-1/
u}$ is convex, non-increasing and bounded by $\mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(2e^u)$, so (b) gives $\|
abla f\|_1 \geq 	frac K2 (1 + \ln 2 + H(f))^{-1/
u}$: this is Proposition ef{tiisent-p} up to the constant, and without the assumption $\|f\|_{\ell^\infty} \leq e^{-1}$.
Under $\mathrm{IS}_d$, the function $\psi(u) := K2^{-1/d}e^{-u/d}$ gives $\|
abla f\|_1 \geq 	frac K2 2^{-1/d} e^{-H(f)/d}$. A group of polynomial growth of degree $d$ has $\mathrm{IS}_d$ and satisfies $H(P^n) \leq 	frac d2 \ln n + C$: this follows from Gibbs' inequality $H(\mu) \leq -\sum_x \mu(x) \ln \sigma(x)$, valid for every probability measure $\sigma$, applied with $\sigma(x)$ proportional to $e^{-|x|/\sqrt n}$ (whose normalising constant is of order $n^{d/2}$), together with $L(n) \preceq \sqrt n$ (see Hebisch \& Saloff-Coste \cite{HSC}). Hence $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq n^{-1/2}$, which is the bound of Corollary ef{tlbgradpol-c} below, with an upper bound on the entropy replacing the lower bound on the return probability used there.
Finally, on every group, the isoperimetric inequality of Coulhon \& Saloff-Coste \cite[Th'eor\`eme 1]{CSC} gives $\mathcal{G}^{\scalebox{.4}{$\searrow$}}(v) \geq c/\Phi(2v)$, where $\Phi$ is the inverse of the growth function, and (a) then yields $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq 1/\Phi ig(4e^{2H(P^n)} ig)$; compare with Corollary ef{cretgrowth}.
head: environment

label: tlbgradpol-c
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{tlbgradpol-c}
If $G$ has polynomial growth of degree $d \geq 2$ (so that its Cayley graphs have $\mathrm{IS}_d$), then $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq K' n^{-1/2}$ for $n$ even.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Under $\mathrm{IS}_d$ with $d \geq 2$, one has $\|\nabla P^n\|_1 \geq \|P^n\|_{d/(d-1)} =: N_d(n)$ (see Woess \cite[4.3 Proposition]{Woe}).
By interpolation,
$\|P^n\|_2 \leq \|P^n\|_{d/(d-1)}^t  \|P^n\|_\infty^{1-t}$
where $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{d-1}{d} t + \frac{1}{\infty} (1-t)$, \emph{i.e.}  $t = \frac{d}{2(d-1)}$ and, consequently, $1-t = \frac{d-2}{2(d-1)}$.
Since, for $n$ even, $\|P^n\|_2^2 = P^{2n}(\mathfr{o}) \asymp n^{-d/2}$ and $\|P^n\|_\infty = P^n(\mathfr{o}) \asymp n^{-d/2}$ (see \emph{e.g.}  \cite{HSC}), this means that
\[
2^{-(d-2)/2}K_1^{d-2-2/d} n^{-1/2} \leq N_d(n) .
\]
Hence, for $n$ even, $\|\nabla P^n\|_1 \geq K_2 n^{-1/2}$, and $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq K_2 n^{-1/2}/|S|$.
head: environment

label: tlbgradc
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{tlbgradc}
Let $X$ be a graph with $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$ (with constant $K$), let $P$ be the transition kernel of a random walk on $X$ and let $o$ be a vertex. Then
\[
 ig\|
abla P^n(o,\cdot) ig\|_{\ell^1} \; \geq \;  rac{K
u}{2^{1/
u}(
u+1)} \, H ig(P^n(o,\cdot) ig)^{-1/
u}
\]
for every $n$ with $\|P^n(o,\cdot)\|_{\ell^\infty} \leq e^{-1}$. If $X$ is a Cayley graph of a group and $P$ is symmetric, this reads
\[
\mathrm{TV}_n \; \geq \;  rac{K
u}{2^{1/
u}(
u+1)\,|S|} \, H(P^n)^{-1/
u},
\]
and the condition on $n$ holds as soon as $n$ is large enough.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first inequality is Proposition \ref{tiisent-p} applied to $f = P^n(o,\cdot)$. On a Cayley graph with $P$ symmetric, $P^n(o,\cdot)$ is the translate of $P^n$ and $\|\nabla P^n\|_{\ell^1} \leq |S|\,\mathrm{TV}_n$ (see \S{}\ref{ssrwtransp}); and $\|P^n\|_{\ell^\infty} \to 0$ since the group is infinite.
head: environment

label: rcretvsiis
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rcretvsiis}
For groups whose volume growth is at least $\mathrm{exp}(cn^
u)$ with $
u \leq 1$ (and which therefore satisfy $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$), Corollary ef{cretgrowth} is never better than Corollary ef{tlbgradc}. Indeed, Peres \& Zheng \cite{PZ} show that on groups a return probability $P^{2n}(\mathfr{o}) \geq \mathrm{exp}(-Cn^\vartheta)$ forces $H(P^n) \preceq n^{\vartheta/(1-\vartheta)}$ (a bound which is only informative for $\vartheta < 1/2$, see Hutchcroft \& Lopez \cite[\S{}1]{HL}). Hence Corollary ef{tlbgradc} gives $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq H(P^n)^{-1/
u} \succeq n^{-\vartheta/((1-\vartheta)
u)}$, which is the bound provided by Corollary ef{cretgrowth} under the same assumptions; and Corollary ef{tlbgradc} is stronger as soon as the entropy grows more slowly than the bound of Peres \& Zheng.
head: environment

label: rentlower
title: Remark
head: environment

label: tlbgradgreen-c
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{tlbgradgreen-c}
Let $g_n$ be as above.
If $G$ has $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$ (\emph{e.g.}  $|B_n| \geq K_1 \mathrm{exp}(K_2n^
u)$ with $
u \leq 1$),
then $\|
abla g_n\|_1 \geq K H(P^n)^{-1/
u}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The main point is an upper bound on $H(g_n)$ (note that $\|g_n\|_{\ell^1} = 1$, and that $\|g_n\|_{\ell^\infty} \leq e^{-1}$ for $n$ large).
For a convex combination of probability measures,
\[
H\Big(\sum_i w_i\mu_i\Big) = \sum_i w_iH(\mu_i) + \sum_i w_i D\Big(\mu_i \,\Big\|\, \sum_j w_j\mu_j\Big),
\]
where $D$ is the Kullback--Leibler divergence. Here $w_i = \tfrac1n$ and $\mu_i = P^i$. Since $g_n \geq \tfrac1n P^i$, each divergence is at most $\ln n$, and $H(P^i) \leq H(P^n)$ as the entropy of the walk is non-decreasing. Hence $H(g_n) \leq H(P^n) + \ln n \leq 2H(P^n)$ for $n$ large, because $H(P^n) \geq -\ln P^{2n}(\mathfr{o})$ grows faster than $\ln n$ under $\mathrm{IIS}_\nu$ (see Remark \ref{rentlower}).
Proposition \ref{tiisent-p} then gives the claim.
head: environment

label: ineqre
title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $q \in \, ]-\infty,1[ \setminus \{0\}$ and $p \in \, ]1,\infty[$. Then
\[\tag{*}\label{ineqre}
                                                                           
H_q(\mu) \geq H(\mu) \geq H_p(\mu) .
\]
Also
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
\displaystyle \lim_{p \to 1^\pm} H_p(\mu) = H(\mu),
& &
\displaystyle \lim_{q \to 0^\pm} H_q(\mu) = \ln \| \mu \|_0,\\[2ex]
\displaystyle  \lim_{q \to +\infty} \frac{\ln \|\mu\|_q^q}{q-1} = \ln \|\mu \|_\infty
& \text{ and } &
\displaystyle  \lim_{q \to -\infty} \frac{\ln \|\mu\|_q^q}{q-1} = \ln \|\mu \|_{-\infty}
\end{array}
\]
where $\| \mu \|_\infty = \sup_x |\mu(x)|$ and $\|\mu\|_{-\infty} = \inf_x \{ |\mu(x)| \mid \mu(x)\neq 0\}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f$ be defined by $f = \mu^q$ for $q \neq 0,1$. Then
\[
H(\mu) = \sum_x \mu(x) (-\ln f(x)^{1/q}) = \frac{1/q}{1-1/q} \sum_x \mu(x) (-\ln f(x)^{1-1/q}) .
\]
If $\frac{1}{q-1} > 0$ (\emph{i.e.}  $q>1$), then use convexity of $x \to -\ln x$ to get
\[
\begin{aligned}
H(\mu) & = \frac{-1}{q-1} \sum_x \mu(x) \ln f(x)^{1-1/q}
\geq \frac{-1}{q-1}  \ln \bigg( \sum_x \mu(x) f(x)^{1-1/q} \bigg) \\
& = \frac{-1}{q-1}  \ln \bigg( \sum_x \mu(x)^q \bigg) ,
\end{aligned}
\]
\emph{i.e.}  $H(\mu) \geq H_q(\mu)$, as desired. If $\frac{1}{q-1} < 0$ (\emph{i.e.}  $q < 1$ and $q \neq 0$), then use concavity of $x \to \ln x$ to get
\[
\begin{aligned}
H(\mu) & = \frac{-1}{q-1} \sum_x \mu(x) \ln f(x)^{1-1/q}
\leq \frac{-1}{q-1}  \ln \bigg( \sum_x \mu(x) f(x)^{1-1/q} \bigg) \\
& = \frac{-1}{q-1}  \ln \bigg( \sum_x \mu(x)^q \bigg) ,
\end{aligned}
\]
\emph{i.e.}  $H(\mu) \leq H_q(\mu)$. For the limit, apply l'H\^opital's rule:
\[
\lim_{p \to 1^\pm} \frac{-\ln \sum_x \mu(x)^p}{p-1}
\overset{H}{=}
\lim_{p \to 1^\pm} - \frac{\sum_x \mu(x)^p \ln \mu(x) }{\|\mu\|^p_p} = \frac{\sum_x \mu(x) (- \ln \mu(x) ) }{\|\mu\|_1} =  H(\mu).
\]
The other limits are also straightforward computations.
head: environment

label: lrenyi
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lrenyi}
If $p<q$, then
\[
H_q(f) \leq H_p(f) .
\]
If further $1<p<q$, then
\[
H_p(f) \leq \tfrac{p(q-1)}{(p-1)q} H_q(f).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall Lyapunov's interpolation inequality: if $q,r \in \, ]-\infty,\infty[$ and $p= \lambda r+ (1-\lambda) q$ (with $\lambda \in \, ]0,1[$), using H\"older with exponent $1/\lambda >1$, one gets
\[
 \int |f|^p =  \int |f|^{\lambda r} |f|^{(1-\lambda)q}  \leq \left( \int |f|^r\right)^\lambda  \left(\int |f|^q\right)^{1-\lambda} = \| f \|_r^{r\lambda} \| f\|_q^{q(1-\lambda)}.
\]
Let us first show that the ratio is monotone on $]1,\infty[$. Assume $p = \theta 1 + (1-\theta)q$, \emph{i.e.}  $\theta = \tfrac{q-p}{q-1}$, then
\[
\|f\|_p^p \leq \|f\|_{1}^{1 \cdot\theta}\cdot\|f\|_{q}^{q(1-\theta)} = \|f\|_{q}^{q(1-\theta)} ,
\]
using $\|f\|_1=1$. Since $1-\theta = \tfrac{1-p}{1-q}$, one has $\ln \|f\|_p^p \leq \tfrac{1-p}{1-q} \ln \|f\|^q_q$ which gives (since $p>1$)
\[
\frac{-\ln \|f\|_p^p}{p-1} \geq \frac{ -\ln \|f\|^q_q}{q-1} .
\]
Next, let us show they are equivalent up to a constant on $]1,\infty[$.
For $p<q$, $\|f\|_p \geq \|f\|_q$ so $ \ln \|f\|_p^p \geq \tfrac{p}{q} \ln \|f\|_q^q$ and so, if $p>1$,
\[
\frac{-\ln \|f\|_p^p}{p-1} \leq \tfrac{p(q-1)}{(p-1)q} \frac{-\ln \|f\|_q^q}{q-1} .
\]
It turns out that using this inequality for $p<1$ is not interesting.
                                                                                                                               
    
                                                                            
    
                                                                    
A better way to finish on the interval $]-\infty,1[$ is to note that Lyapunov's inequality still holds: $\ln \|f\|_p^p \leq \tfrac{1-p}{1-q} \ln \|f\|^q_q$ if $p>q$. This time $q<p<1$, so
\[
\frac{\ln \|f\|_p^p}{1-p} \leq \frac{\ln \|f\|^q_q}{1-q}. \qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
It is interesting to notice that each of these functions is, up to a logarithm and a sign, a R\'enyi entropy, namely:\\
\textbullet $H_0(P^n)$ is the logarithm of the growth function.\\
\textbullet $H_1(P^n)$ is the entropy.\\
\textbullet $H_2(P^n)$ is minus the logarithm of the return probability at time $2n$.\\
\textbullet $H_\infty(P^n)$ is minus the logarithm of the return probability.\\
This is noteworthy in view of Question \ref{qrent}. The logarithms may look artificial, but the logarithm of the growth function (resp. minus the logarithm of the return probability) are subadditive functions.
head: environment

label: quesentgro
title: Question
head: environment

label: rrevpinskerfolk
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rrevpinskerfolk}
For a group with $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$, Proposition ef{prevpinsker} and Corollary ef{tlbgradc} give two lower bounds on the total variation profile, $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$ and $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq H(P^n)^{-1/
u}$. Deciding whether the first one always beats the second one, \emph{i.e.}  whether
\[	ag{$\dagger$}
H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n) \; \succeq \; H(P^n)^{-1/
u},
\]
amounts to answering Question ef{quesentgro}.2 (with $v = 
u$), and in particular, for groups of exponential growth (which satisfy $\mathrm{IIS}_1$), to deciding the folklore conjecture.
Indeed, put $q := 1 + 	frac1
u$. If $H(P^{k+1}) - H(P^k) \geq c\, H(P^k)^{-1/
u}$ for all $k$, then the convexity of $x \mapsto x^q$ gives
\[
H(P^{k+1})^q - H(P^k)^q \; \geq \; q\, H(P^k)^{q-1} ig(H(P^{k+1}) - H(P^k) ig) \; \geq \; qc ,
\]
and summing over $k$ yields $H(P^n)^q \succeq n$, \emph{i.e.}  $H(P^n) \succeq n^{
u/(
u+1)}$. Conversely, if $H(P^n) \asymp n^\eta$ with $\eta \geq 
u/(
u+1)$, then, the increments being non-increasing, $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n) \geq  rac{H(P^{Kn}) - H(P^n)}{(K-1)n} \succeq n^{\eta-1} \succeq H(P^n)^{-1/
u}$ for a fixed $K$ large enough. The two statements are thus equivalent, up to the regularity of $n \mapsto H(P^n)$.
Since a group of growth at least $\mathrm{exp}(n^
u)$ satisfies $\mathrm{IIS}_
u$ for $
u \leq 1$ (see \S{}ef{ssiis}), a positive answer to ($\dagger$) would therefore give strong support to Grigorchuk's gap conjecture \cite{Gri-gap}: it would imply its weak form described above.
In other words, by the computation above, a group whose growth is of the form $\mathrm{exp}(n^v)$ with $v < 1/2$ would be a counterexample to ($\dagger$) with $
u = v$.
head: environment

label: lquot
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lquot}
Let $\pi : G \to Q$ be onto, $P$ a finitely supported measure on $G$ and $\pi_*P$ the push-forward measure on $Q$. Then $\mathrm{TV}_n(P) \geq \mathrm{TV}_n(\pi_*P)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The push-forward $\pi_*P$ is a finitely supported probability measure on $Q$, its convolution powers are the push-forwards $\pi_*(P^n)$, and $\pi_*(\delta_s * P^n) = \delta_{\pi(s)} * \pi_*(P^n)$. Since push-forwards do not increase the total variation distance, the total variation profile of $(G,P,S)$ dominates that of $(Q, \pi_*P, \pi(S))$.
head: environment

label: exz2z2
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exz2z2}
Consider the lazy simple random walk on $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}/2\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) \wr \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ with respect to the standard generators (switch the lamp at the position of the lamplighter, or move the lamplighter), and let $R_n$ be the range of the lamplighter up to time $n$. Then $H(P^n) \asymp \mathbbold{E}|R_n|$. For the lower bound, condition on the trajectory of the lamplighter: the lamp states at distinct visited sites are then independent, and a positive proportion of them are non-degenerate, so conditioning (which does not increase entropy) gives $H(P^n) \geq c\,\mathbbold{E}|R_n|$. For the upper bound, $X_n$ is determined by its position, the range and the lamp states on the range, and the number of connected subsets of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ of size $k$ containing the origin is at most exponential in $k$, so $H(P^n) \leq C\,\mathbbold{E}|R_n| + C\ln n$. By Dvoretzky \& Erd\H{o}s \cite{DE}, $\mathbbold{E}|R_n| \asymp n/\ln n$. These lamplighters go back to Kaimanovich \& Vershik \cite[\S{}6]{KV}, and the asymptotics of their entropy are well known (see Erschler \cite{Ers-drift}, and Benjamini, Duminil-Copin, Kozma \& Yadin \cite[Proposition 13]{BDKY-lamp}, where iterated wreath products are also treated); the argument above is recalled for completeness.

Since the increments are non-increasing, $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n) \geq \frac{H(P^{Kn}) - H(P^n)}{(K-1)n}$ for every integer $K \geq 2$, and the two-sided bound $H(P^n) \asymp n/\ln n$ makes the right-hand side $\succeq 1/\ln n$ for a fixed $K$ large enough. Proposition \ref{prevpinsker} therefore gives
\[
\frac{1}{\ln n} \; \preceq \; \mathrm{TV}_n \; \preceq \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{\ln n}} ,
\]
the upper bound coming from the entropy-increment inequality. For comparison, Corollary \ref{tlbgradc} (which applies with $\nu = 2$, see \S{}\ref{ssiis}) only gives $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq \sqrt{\ln n / n}$, and Proposition \ref{ptvspeed} only gives $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq \ln n / n$.
head: environment

label: excf
title: Example
body_md:
\label{excf}
Let $G$ be a group of exponential growth with controlled F\o lner pairs (see Tessera \cite[Definition 4.8]{Tes-iso}).
The results of Coulhon, Grigor'yan \& Pittet \cite{CGP}, which also apply to graphs, can be used to show that $P^{2n}(\mathfr{o}) \geq \mathrm{exp}(-Cn^{1/3})$, the slowest decay allowed by exponential growth.
Hence Corollary \ref{cretgrowth} gives $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq n^{-1/2}$ (and so does Corollary \ref{tlbgradc}, see Remark \ref{rcretvsiis}), while the bound $H(P^n) \preceq \sqrt n$ of Peres \& Zheng \cite{PZ} and the entropy-increment inequality give $\mathrm{TV}_n \preceq n^{-1/4}$. On $F \wr \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, the argument of Example \ref{exz2z2} shows that $H(P^n)$ is comparable to the expected range of the lamplighter, so that $H(P^n) \asymp \sqrt n$ and Proposition \ref{prevpinsker} also gives $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq n^{-1/2}$.
For $F \wr \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ this is the right order, at least for the switch-walk-switch measure (switch the lamp at the position of the lamplighter to a uniform element of $F$, make a step of the lazy simple random walk on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, and switch again). Indeed, conditionally on the trajectory $(x_k)$ of the lamplighter, the lamps on its range are then independent and uniform, the others being trivial. So left multiplication by a lamp generator, which only modifies the lamp at the origin, leaves $P^n$ unchanged, while $\|\delta_t * P^n - P^n\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$, for the position generator $t$, is at most the total variation distance between the law of $\big(\min_{k \leq n} x_k, \max_{k \leq n} x_k, x_n\big)$ and its translate,
               
which is $O(n^{-1/2})$ by the reflection principle and the local limit theorem. With Lemma \ref{lquot}, $\mathrm{TV}_n \asymp n^{-1/2}$: the total variation profile of $F \wr \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ is that of its projection to $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$.

label: rfloor
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rfloor}
There are currently no realisation theorems (like the construction of prescribed speed, entropy and isoperimetric profiles of Brieussel \& Zheng \cite{BZ}) for $\mathrm{TV}_n$, so which functions occur is open.

The bound $n^{-1/2}$ looks like a floor. On groups of polynomial growth there are many ways to see this (\emph{e.g.}  Corollary \ref{tlbgradpol-c}), and by Proposition \ref{ptvspeed} it holds whenever the walk is diffusive.
                                                                                                                                 
Corollaries \ref{cretgrowth} and \ref{tlbgradc} give it when the volume growth is at least $\mathrm{exp}(cn^\nu)$ and the return probability decays as slowly as this growth allows, \emph{i.e.}  $P^{2n}(\mathfr{o}) \geq \mathrm{exp}(-Cn^{\nu/(\nu+2)})$.
This covers the groups of Example \ref{excf}.
The floor also holds on every group with an infinite virtually nilpotent quotient, by Lemma \ref{lquot} and Proposition \ref{ptvspeed} applied on the quotient, where the walk is diffusive (see Hebisch \& Saloff-Coste \cite{HSC}).
                                                                                                                                            

Our lower bounds restrict the groups on which this floor could fail. Assume, to fix ideas, that $L(n) \asymp n^\beta$ and $H(P^n) \asymp n^\eta$, and let $\nu$ be such that the group has $\mathrm{IIS}_\nu$. Proposition \ref{ptvspeed} gives the floor unless $\beta > 1/2$. Proposition \ref{prevpinsker} gives it unless $\eta < 1/2$, the increments of the entropy being then of order $n^{\eta - 1}$ by concavity (as in Example \ref{exz2z2}). Corollary \ref{tlbgradc} gives it unless $\eta > \nu/2$. Hence a group on which the floor fails satisfies $\nu/2 < \eta < 1/2 < \beta$. In particular $\nu < 1$, so the group does not have $\mathrm{IIS}_1$; as groups of exponential growth have $\mathrm{IIS}_1$ and groups of polynomial growth satisfy the floor, it has intermediate growth. Moreover, as recalled above, $L(n)^2 \preceq n\, H(P^n)$ by the Varopoulos--Carne estimate, whence $\beta \leq (1+\eta)/2 < 3/4$, and by the previous paragraph the group has no infinite virtually nilpotent quotient. Put differently, on every group with $\mathrm{IIS}_1$ (for instance of exponential growth) whose entropy grows like a power, the floor holds: Corollary \ref{tlbgradc} (with $\nu = 1$) gives it when $\eta \leq 1/2$, and Proposition \ref{prevpinsker} when $\eta \geq 1/2$.

This applies in particular to the first Grigorchuk group. Its simple random walk is superdiffusive, $n^{1/(2\alpha_0)} \preceq L(n) \preceq n^{3/4}$ where $\alpha_0 \approx 0.767$ is the exponent of its growth, so that Proposition \ref{ptvspeed} does not give the floor; but its F\o lner function is at least exponential (see Erschler \& Zheng \cite[Example 1.3]{EZ-iso}), \emph{i.e.}  it has $\mathrm{IIS}_1$ (see Zheng \cite[Propositions 1.4 and 1.5]{Zheng-Grig}). Likewise, the finitely generated simple amenable groups of Juschenko \& Monod \cite{JM}, namely the derived subgroups of topological full groups of minimal subshifts, have exponential growth by Matui \cite[Corollary 2.5]{Matui}. The question thus remains open only for groups which, together with all their infinite quotients, have intermediate growth without $\mathrm{IIS}_1$, a superdiffusive speed (though slower than $n^{3/4}$) and an entropy growing more slowly than $\sqrt n$, \emph{i.e.}  with a significant gap between entropy and speed. The author knows of no group on which $\mathrm{TV}_n \succeq n^{-1/2}$ fails.

label: qrent
title: Question
body_md:
\label{qrent}
Assume $G$ is a group of exponential growth. Is the function $n \mapsto H_0(P^{2n})$ concave? In other words, is the function $n \mapsto \ln |B_{2n}|$ (where $B_n$ are the balls of radius $n$) concave?

body_md: How many different equivalence classes of functions are there in the sequence $H_p(P^n)$ where $-\infty \leq p < 1$?

label: rrenyismallp
title: Remark
head: environment
